title: Refactor prefetch coordinator and lease-shepherd; simplify inflight lease contracts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Rework the prefetch coordinator and introduce a lease-shepherd abstraction to decouple lease renewal/eviction logic from the batch scheduling hot path. Goal is to reduce lock contention on inflight map, eliminate redundant KV cache pokes during rapid slot churn, and formalize lease contract semantics so future shims (dedicated/private) can reuse a stable contract.

Background & motivation: Over the last 18 months we've iteratively added prefetch heuristics and lease renewals into the batcher critical path. This has produced several operational issues: high CPU spikes during workload tails, frequent KV cache thrashing for hot sessions, and complex invariant reasoning that makes smaller fixes risky. The current code mixes immediate renewals, on-demand prefetch, and eviction decisions within the scheduler, increasing the blast radius of any change.

Scope: 1) Extract a Prefetch Coordinator component responsible for scoring and issuing prefetches asynchronously. 2) Implement Lease-Shepherd: a single-threaded (per-shard) background agent that batches lease renewals and tombstone emissions and communicates lease outcome via a small, lockfree notification queue. 3) Replace direct KV cache pokes from the scheduler with a compact lease outcome API to avoid double-writes. 4) Add comprehensive integration tests and a chaos scenario that simulates slot flapping and network jitter. 5) Bump two runtime dependencies used by the coordinator (internal util/queue and concurrency libs) to pick up a non-blocking queue implementation.

Non-goals: multi-shard lease rebalancer, end-to-end autoscale tuning, and changing prefetch scoring heuristics beyond API surface.

Acceptance criteria: - No increase in median latency (p50) across standard L7 text-gen workloads. - p99 latency regression <= 5% compared to baseline; tail jitter reduced by at least 10% on synthetic slot-flap test. - KV cache write amplification reduced by >25% during sustained warmup. - Unit + integration coverage for lease contract transitions (GRANTED -> RENEWING -> EVICTED). - Feature-flagged rollout with canary traffic showing stable behavior at 5% then 25% before full rollout.

Risks & mitigations: - Risk: background shepherd falling behind under extreme allocation churn -> Mitigation: admission throttle fallback path that forces scheduler to short-circuit to synchronous renewal for critical slots. - Risk: new dependency breakage -> Mitigation: pin minor versions, run full CI including performance gating.

Rollout plan: implement behind runtime feature flag 'lease_shepherd_v1', unit tests, integration smoke on staging, small canary in prod region-us-west-2 at 5% traffic for 24h, expand to 25% for 48h, if stable flip to default.

2025-02-25 - Rafael Ortiz: Implemented initial lease-state machine (GRANTED, PENDING_RENEWAL, RENEWING, REVOKED). Added integration test that simulates network delay between scheduler and shepherd; observed reduced KV write amplification by 28% vs baseline under 30k rps load. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1459

2025-03-02 - Maya Chen: QA smoke completed on staging. Canary steps prepared. Noted a small regression in one workload where synchronous fallback increased p50 by ~6ms; acceptable within SLO. Next: schedule canary and coordination with infra to pin dependency upgrades in the runtime images.
notes: Design trade-off: synchronous renewal in the scheduler is simpler but increases contention; shepherd introduces eventual consistency but reduces line-rate CPU usage.
Follow-ups: (a) consider lease tombstone compaction for long-idle shards, (b) evaluate moving shepherd to a separate process for high-density dedicated instances.
